skill.name: azure-functions
skill.description: Expert patterns for Azure Functions development including isolated worker model, Durable Functions orchestration, cold start optimization, and production patterns. Covers .NET, Python, and Node.js programming models. Use when: azure function, azure functions, durable functions, azure serverless, function app.
skill.summary: Guidance for designing, reviewing, and hardening Azure Functions applications.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: No static findings were reported, and the reviewed SKILL.md contains only Azure Functions guidance. No prompt injection, data exfiltration intent, executable code, or tool-abuse instructions were found.

content.value_statement: Azure Functions projects can fail from runtime choices, cold starts, and async mistakes. This skill gives focused guidance for safer serverless design and production review.
actual_capabilities: Explains the .NET isolated worker model for modern Azure Functions projects.
Covers the Node.js v4 programming model for TypeScript and JavaScript functions.
Covers the Python v2 decorator-based programming model.
Identifies common anti-patterns such as blocking async calls and per-request HTTP clients.
Highlights operational issues such as timeouts, Application Insights, extension bundles, and warmup triggers.
Supports Durable Functions planning and cold start optimization guidance.
limitations: It provides guidance only and does not deploy or modify Azure resources.
It does not replace official Azure documentation for current platform limits or pricing.
It does not include runnable project templates, scripts, or generated infrastructure files.
Precise recommendations require project details from the user.

use_cases.title: Modernize Function Apps
use_cases.description: Choose the right Azure Functions programming model for a new or migrated project.

use_cases.title: Plan Durable Workflows
use_cases.description: Map long-running serverless work into orchestration, activity, retry, and monitoring patterns.

use_cases.title: Review Production Readiness
use_cases.description: Check a Function App design for cold starts, timeouts, monitoring, and async risks.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Programming Model
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning a new Azure Functions project.
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain which Azure Functions programming model fits my new project. I use [language], [trigger type], and [hosting plan].

prompt_templates.title: Review Function Design
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Azure Functions design for async behavior, HTTP client usage, timeout risk, and monitoring gaps. Recommend concrete changes.

prompt_templates.title: Design Durable Orchestration
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Durable Functions workflow for [business process]. Include orchestration boundaries, retries, idempotency, and observability concerns.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Production Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit my production Function App architecture for cold starts, extension bundle issues, runtime model choices, Application Insights, and scaling risks.

output_examples.input: I am starting a .NET Function App with HTTP triggers and queue processing.
output: Use the isolated worker model for a new .NET project.
Keep request handling asynchronous throughout the call path.
Plan monitoring and timeout behavior before choosing a hosting plan.

output_examples.input: My HTTP-triggered function is slow after idle periods.
output: Review cold start causes before changing business logic.
Consider warmup triggers where the hosting plan supports them.
Check dependency initialization and Application Insights telemetry.

output_examples.input: I need a reliable workflow for multi-step order processing.
output: Use Durable Functions for orchestration and retry control.
Separate orchestration decisions from activity work.
Design idempotent activities before adding external integrations.

best_practices: Share HTTP clients or use factory patterns to avoid socket exhaustion.
Use the isolated worker model for new .NET function projects.
Configure monitoring, timeouts, and warmup behavior before production release.
anti_patterns: Do not block asynchronous calls inside function handlers.
Do not create a new HTTP client for every request.
Do not choose the in-process .NET model for new projects.
